x: Charlie Smart adopted his usual forcing tactics and took the field along at a good pace. With a mile to go Furze, of the Poly, went ahead; with McIntyre, of Achilles, and Smart next, while H.

Also the field was a really “hot” one, the Achilles team being Ward, McIntyre and Ellis, while the Poly. had Reeve, Furze and Stockwell, and there were, of course, the Birchfield boys to be considered.

Walker set off on the last stage, in the company of Sale and Milner, to gain third place, but was well below his best and not only did he have to give way to his two opponents but Chelmsford (Hill - Cottingham) and Ponders End (McIntyre) rubbed it in by passing him in the last half-mile.
At the end of the first lap of the country Dick Tobin was in front of a small bunch which included Clough and McIntyre (Southern Champion) of Thames and Carter and F.P.
